利.meaning: A castaway on a tiny island has one trick. He cuts a stalk of <part>grain</part> with his <part>dagger</part>, bakes a single bread roll on a hot stone and sells it to a hungry passing sailor for a gold coin. Five stalks, five rolls, five coins. He's turning a <kanji>profit</kanji>.
利.on: He hides his coins in a sunken chest out on the coral <sound>ree</sound>f, where only the fish can see them.
利.kun: A sailor tries to pick the chest's lock with a fishbone, but only the castaway's own <sound>key</sound> does the job: it works.

戚.meaning: Every winter the whole family crowds round a <part>candlestick</part> while Grandpa passes round his old <part>battle axe</part>. Each newcomer, babies included, gets a name scratched into its handle, until the wood is covered in names. Everyone carved on it is one of your <kanji>relatives</kanji>.
戚.on: The handle gets so crowded that Grandpa draws a pie chart on it: each branch of the family gets its own <sound>sec</sound>tor.
戚.kun: When Grandpa's own name is carved at last, the room goes quiet. '<sound>Ee</sound>…' whimpers a little cousin, too sad even to finish her <sound>ta</sound>co.

橋.meaning: A cat is stuck on the roof of a <part>skyscraper</part>, staring at the park across the road. A storm blows the tallest <part>tree</part> in the park over, and it crashes down with its top branches resting on the roof. The cat strolls across the trunk to the other side. It's a <kanji>bridge</kanji>.
橋.on: The trunk is so long the cat ends up in <sound>Kyo</sound>to, purring the start of the name all the way over, slow and drawn out.
橋.kun: A shepherd builds a <sound>hu</sound>t at one end of the trunk and herds his <sound>shee</sound>p over it, one by one.

別.meaning: A cake sits in a paper <part>wrap</part>, and a greedy <part>mouth</part> waits on top of it, drooling. To stop a fight, Mum takes a <part>dagger</part> and cuts it straight down the middle, then sends each twin to opposite ends of the house with their half. Now they're <kanji>separate</kanji>.
別.on: From their rooms, the twins place <sound>bets</sound> on whose half had more icing.
別.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' cries one twin, waving goodbye to the other with a <sound>ca</sound>rp-shaped flag: time to part.

駐.meaning: A tired <part>horse</part> carries a <part>lord</part> across the desert, then plants its hooves at an oasis and refuses to take one more step. Fine, sighs the lord, one night here and then we ride on. It's only a <kanji>stop-over</kanji>.
駐.on: By morning the horse has stuck <sound>chew</sound>ing gum all over the saddle, so they can't leave at all.

原.meaning: From the top of a <part>cliff</part>, a girl blows on a <part>white</part> dandelion clock and the seeds float down into the empty valley below. One <part>little</part> sprout pops up, then a thousand. By summer the whole valley is a sea of grass and wildflowers, buzzing with bees. It's a <kanji>meadow</kanji>.
原.on: <sound>Gen</sound>, the hiker who found the spring, wanders down and lies in the long grass for a nap.
原.kun: Gen builds a little <sound>hu</sound>t in the meadow, and the bees buzz round it cheering '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

産.meaning: On a <part>stand</part> at the very edge of a <part>cliff</part>, a farmer sets out everything that springs to <part>life</part> in her garden: carrots, melons, pumpkins, plums. Hang gliders swoop past and buy as they fly. Grown right here, it's fresh <kanji>produce</kanji>.
産.on: One hang glider buys a strawberry <sound>sun</sound>dae, piled high with fruit fresh from the stand.
産.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>!' gasps the farmer, as her goat gives birth to twins right under the stand.

美.meaning: A sculptor carves a <part>large</part> statue of a man with a curly <part>ram's head</part>. At first the whole village laughs at it. But at sunrise the gold horns catch the light, and the crowd falls silent. It's pure <kanji>beauty</kanji>.
美.on: A shiny green <sound>bee</sound>tle lands on one horn and sparkles like a jewel.
美.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps the crowd, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the sculptor in the stone dust, and a <sound>coo</sound>k drops his pan to stare.

術.meaning: At a busy <part>crossroads</part>, a juggler plucks the single apple off a scrawny <part>apple tree</part>, tosses it up with two knives and catches it peeled, cored and sliced. Cars stop to honk and clap. Years of practice went into that: it's <kanji>art</kanji>.
術.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of pigeons gives him top marks, and one sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' on the apple peel.
術.kun: His only means of making a living: juggling <sound>su</sound>shi on the corner, then sleeping in a <sound>be</sound>d of apple peel.

箱.meaning: Two beavers on opposite banks gnaw <part>bamboo</part> canes and weave them into walls, each one copying the other across the river in <part>mutual</part> silence. They meet in the middle, slot their two halves together and tie a lid on top. It's a <kanji>box</kanji>.
箱.on: They pack a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p inside, because beavers like to keep clean.
箱.kun: They post the box to a <sound>hu</sound>t in the woods, where a <sound>ko</sound>ala opens it and washes its paws.

痢.meaning: The castaway who turned a <part>profit</part> on bread rolls eats the last stale one himself. All night long he dashes back and forth to the <part>leaky shed</part> behind his camp, drips plopping on his head, tummy gurgling. He's got <kanji>diarrhea</kanji>.
痢.on: He spends the next day lying weak on the warm <sound>ree</sound>f, swearing never to eat bread again.

算.meaning: A shopkeeper builds an abacus from thin <part>bamboo</part> rods and props it up on a little <part>goal</part> frame. With one sharp <part>eye</part> on the beads, she clicks them back and forth, adding up the whole day's takings in seconds. She can <kanji>calculate</kanji> anything.
算.on: Then she works out exactly how many cherries go on each ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae.
算.kun: She does her sums lying on a <sound>so</sound>fa, while a <sound>ro</sound>dent slides the beads for her.

精.meaning: In a jeweller's window, on <part>blue</part> velvet, lie a hundred grains of <part>rice</part>, polished one by one until they shine like tiny pearls. The price tag has a lot of zeros. Nothing in the shop is more <kanji>refined</kanji>.
精.on: At night the jeweller locks the rice away in a heavy steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
精.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p rubs each grain with its wool, and the jeweller cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': polished to a shine.

趣.meaning: A <part>runner</part> races through a library that closes in five minutes. From each book she has time to <part>take</part> just one line as she flies past the shelves. At the door, panting, she can tell you what every book was about: its <kanji>purport</kanji>.
趣.on: She keeps going on a <sound>su</sound>gar cube tucked in her cheek.
趣.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps at the last book, where a <sound>mo</sound>le and a <sound>moo</sound>se share the <sound>key</sound> to a secret garden. What charm.

誕.meaning: The mayor's <part>speech</part> drags on and on, and each time he nearly stops, he finds a way to <part>prolong</part> it. Halfway through, a woman in the front row gasps, and a baby is born right there in the hall. Nobody remembers the speech: everyone talks about the <kanji>nativity</kanji>.
誕.on: The baby is rushed home through a long dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, crying the whole way.

除.meaning: A tour guide waves her <part>pennant</part> at the boat dock. Forty tourists, thirty seats: that's <part>too much</part>. She points the flag at the last ten in line and shakes her head. To fit on the boat, she has to <kanji>exclude</kanji> them.
除.on: One of them is a <sound>jo</sound>gger, who just runs along the bank beside the boat.
除.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' cries a fortune-teller left on the dock, shaking her <sound>zo</sound>diac chart. She's removed anyway.

掃.meaning: A ship's cook ties a <part>feather duster</part> to the ship's <part>anchor</part> and drops it overboard. As the ship drifts, it drags along the seabed, brushing the sand off old coins and sleepy crabs. Swish, swish: he's found a way to <kanji>sweep</kanji> the ocean floor.
掃.on: Then he scrubs the deck with a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p until the foam spills over the side.
掃.kun: The duster bumps into a tiny <sound>hu</sound>t on the seabed and sweeps its doorstep too.

画.meaning: An octopus paints on the harbour wall: <part>one</part> long line for the sea, then a jar with a stem in the middle, for no <part>reason</part> at all. It dips each arm in a <part>bucket</part> of ink first. Eight arms, eight swishes, each one a perfect <kanji>brush-stroke</kanji>.
画.on: Then it paints a bulb of <sound>gar</sound>lic, so real that passing fish stop to sniff it.
画.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp swims up to look, and a <sound>coo</sound>k on the pier draws a chalk line round the painting: marked off.

司.meaning: On a film set, a bossy woman perches on a <part>crowbar</part> bent into a tall chair. From her <part>mouth</part> comes just <part>one</part> word, 'Action!', and a hundred people leap into motion. She's the <kanji>director</kanji>.
司.on: When the stunt goes wrong, she ducks behind a knight's <sound>shie</sound>ld from the props table.
司.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, then orders a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>do</sound>lphin to their places: she rules the set.

寿.meaning: A tortoise turns a hundred and throws a party on the golf course. It swings its <part>golf club</part> beside a cake with <part>three</part> tiers, and one <part>slash</part> of the knife cuts the first slice. Here's to a hundred more: <kanji>longevity</kanji>!
寿.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of old turtles agrees it's the oldest guest they've ever seen.
寿.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala carves it a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, a friend gives it a <sound>boo</sound>k, and the mayor hands over a golden <sound>key</sound>.

科.meaning: In a big store, a sign hangs over one aisle: here everything is sold by the <part>ladle</part>. Shoppers scoop <part>grain</part>, oats, flour and lentils from tall barrels into paper bags. It's the bulk food <kanji>department</kanji>.
科.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in a tank by the till gobbles every grain that spills.

百.meaning: A chef separates egg <part>white</part> from yolk, <part>one</part> egg at a time, for the world's biggest meringue. Her arm aches and the bowl overflows. She drops the last shell on the pile and counts: she's cracked a <kanji>hundred</kanji>.
百.on: '<sound>Hee</sound>… <sound>yuck</sound>!' she giggles, wiping sticky egg off her nose.
百.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le on a <sound>mo</sound>tor scooter delivers another hundred eggs.

貨.meaning: At the docks, crates of <part>shellfish</part> are loaded onto a ship. Halfway across the sea, they <part>change</part> into crates of pearls and coins. Whatever is inside, the captain doesn't care: to him, it's all just <kanji>freight</kanji>.
貨.on: He stamps every crate with a big orange <sound>ca</sound>rp, his ship's badge.
貨.kun: A deckhand opens one and finds a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a crown, and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': treasure!

死.meaning: A skeleton chef, all <part>bones</part>, stirs a pot of soup with a long <part>spoon</part> and lifts it to taste. No tongue, no taste. 'Needs salt,' he guesses, and shrugs. That's the trouble with <kanji>death</kanji>.
死.on: He serves the soup on a knight's <sound>shie</sound>ld, since all his plates broke long ago.
死.kun: His only customer is the ghost of a <sound>shee</sound>p, who has been dead for years.

解.meaning: A <part>cow</part> wanders through a knitting shop and comes out wrapped in yarn from nose to <part>antler</part>. The owner slips a <part>sword</part> under one loop and tugs, and the knot starts to come loose, strand by strand. Slowly, she manages to <kanji>unravel</kanji> it.
解.on: Inside the tangle she finds a lost <sound>ki</sound>te, and lets it fly.
解.kun: The last strand comes off a <sound>to</sound>tem pole the cow had dragged in with it.

過.meaning: A <part>cuckoo clock</part> should call noon twelve times. This one calls a hundred, then a thousand, until it shakes itself off the wall and bounces down a <part>ramp</part>, still shouting. It always has to <kanji>overdo</kanji> it.
過.on: At the bottom it splashes into a pond, where a <sound>ca</sound>rp sits on it until it stops.
過.kun: On its way down, it rolls right past a <sound>su</sound>shi stall without stopping.

憩.meaning: A tired dragon lies on the castle lawn with its <part>tongue</part> hanging out, letting out slow puffs of smoky <part>breath</part>. No knights, no fire, no treasure, just ten quiet minutes in the sun. It's taking a <kanji>recess</kanji>.
憩.on: A knight sneaks up, not to fight, but to share a slice of <sound>ca</sound>ke.
憩.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>…' the dragon sighs, as a <sound>ko</sound>ala curls up on its warm belly to nap too.

矛.meaning: The castle guard knew the dragon was coming, so she got her weapon ready <part>beforehand</part>: a long pole with a pointed blade, plus a hook on the side for one last <part>slash</part>. She waits at the gate long before the roar. She holds a <kanji>halberd</kanji>.
矛.on: But it's only a <sound>moo</sound>se that wanders in, bowing politely.
矛.kun: After the scare, she hangs it in the <sound>ho</sound>tel lobby, where a <sound>ko</sound>ala uses it to scratch its back.

野.meaning: A farmer plans every row of her <part>farm</part> <part>beforehand</part>: neat lines of cabbages, all straight. One morning her goat eats the fence, and wild grass rolls in from the hills. Now it's open, rustic <kanji>plains</kanji> as far as she can see.
野.on: The goat ambles off across the grass, trailing a ball of <sound>yar</sound>n behind it.
野.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' shouts the farmer, chasing it across the field.

菜.meaning: In a strange garden, you roll the <part>dice</part> on the <part>grass</part> and dig where they stop. A six: a carrot. A two: a turnip. A one: a giant leek. Whatever you pull up, it's a <kanji>vegetable</kanji>.
菜.on: Roll a double and you also win a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der.
菜.kun: You wrap your whole harvest in a warm <sound>na</sound>an and eat it in the grass.
